cases.name: uses parentheses to force the addition first

exercise2.hint: Without parentheses Python multiplies before it adds, so 10 + 5 * 3 - 8 gives 17. The parentheses are what make the addition happen first.

questions.explain: A single slash always gives a float, even when the numbers divide evenly.
Double slash is floor division: it divides and discards the remainder.
The modulo operator gives the remainder. It is how you test whether a number divides evenly.
Multiplication binds tighter than addition, so this is 2 + 12. Parentheses are how you override that.

questions.prompt: How do you make the addition happen first?
questions.explain: Parentheses are evaluated first, which is the P in PEMDAS.

questions.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning.
right: Division rounded down to the floor
questions.explain: /: Division that returns a quotient. //: Division rounded down to the floor. %: Remainder after floor division.

questions.prompt: Arrange these steps in the intended order.
questions.explain: Each calculation depends on a value defined earlier; the final remainder is 2.

questions.label: Predict the first line of output (without surrounding quotes).
questions.prompt:
items = 17
box_size = 5
print(items // box_size)
print(items % box_size)
print(items / box_size)

First output line: ___
questions.explain: Three complete boxes hold 15 items, with 2 left over. Check the relationship 17 == 3 * 5 + 2. The ordinary quotient 3.4 is useful as a ratio, but it is not a count of complete boxes.
